claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. Let me ask you a few questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, it's a bit complicated. Alex has been in local authority care for a few months now, and he stays there full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand, thank you for sharing that. Let me just read up on the specific rules around Child Benefit when a child is in local authority care to make sure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a couple more questions to clarify the situation.

You mentioned Alex has been in local authority care for a few months. Has Alex been in care for more than 8 weeks continuously?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he's been there for about 3 months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks, there's an important question I need to ask:

Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you? For example, does he come home for regular visits that total at least 24 hours each week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home that often. He stays at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have one more question: Does Alex spend either 2 nights in a row each week at home with you, or 7 or more days in a row at home at any time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't. He stays at the care home all the time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all the information you've provided. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex:**
- Alex has been in local authority care for approximately 3 months, which is longer than the 8-week threshold.
- Under the Child Benefit rules, you're usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit after a child has been in care for more than 8 weeks.
- There are exceptions that would allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit, such as if Alex spends at least 24 hours a week at home, or if he spends 2 consecutive nights per week or 7 or more consecutive days at home. Unfortunately, since Alex stays at the care home full-time, these exceptions don't apply.

**What you should know:**
- If Alex's circumstances change in the future and he starts spending more time at home (either 24+ hours per week, 2 consecutive nights per week, or 7+ consecutive days), you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to contact HMRC to find out what to do next.

I understand this may not be the news you were hoping for. If you have any questions or if Alex's situation changes, please don't hesitate to get in touch with the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.

The claimant has confirmed that Alex stays at the care home full-time and does not meet either of these exceptions. Therefore, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
